verdict: Existing requested-Layout Vec growth and conservative overlap formulas remain valid for the inspected runtime call paths; no formula change indicated by these alloc-source differences. This does not certify the complete allocation_schedule or production resources.

evidence.claim: RawVec minimum capacities and amortized growth unchanged: 8 for1-byte elements,4 for size<=1024,1 otherwise; new=max(2*old,len+additional,minimum). Runtime reserve forwards unchanged. Functions moved into const-capable impls without changing this arithmetic.

extend_from_slice on u8/u64 selects trivial-clone slice specialization; append_elements still calls reserve(slice.len()) exactly once. 1.99 factors copying into append_elements_unreserved and adds fallible helpers; unchanged successful requested capacities.

Generic extend reserves lower.size_hint+1 only on full buffer; TrustedLen reserves exact additional. SpecFromIterNested is byte-for-byte unchanged. SpecFromIter changes only core::ptr import. IntoIter extension now accepts any allocator and eagerly deallocates source after append; it does not increase requested output capacity.

Global runtime allocate returns requested Layout size; runtime grow with same alignment forwards new Layout size to realloc_nonnull. Different-alignment branch allocates new then copies/deallocates old. Const/runtime dispatch additions do not change these runtime branches. RawVec keeps element alignment fixed.
frame_bytes starts empty; Vec Sink uses extend_from_slice for begin prefixes(2,taglen,2), and each field(4,len). This is exactly frame_allocation parts.

encode_words begins with5 words then exact map/slice appends; final capacity <=max(minimum,2*final_length), including initial capacity5. crt_bytes borrows that word Vec while collecting bytes, so both serializations coexist. Generic/TrustedLen collection both stay within grow-only bound because valid size-hint reservation never exceeds final length. Borrowed iterator does not reuse owning-Vec allocation.

proof_notes: For every growing reserve, new>=2*old and new<=max(minimum,2*final_length), since old<required<=final_length. Therefore old<=floor(new/2), and C+floor(C/2) upper-bounds concurrent old/new requested layouts for C=max(minimum,2*final_length).

vec_append_schedule models exact successful reserve requests for the specified append sequence, with initial representing an initially full buffer(length=capacity), not arbitrary spare capacity. Its sum_requested_bytes is cumulative request volume and must not be described as peak or physical allocation.
No dynamic allocation benchmark or compiler test was run by this reviewer. Root owns separate current-toolchain provider layout probes.
limitations: Only allocator policy assumptions of allocation_schedule were reviewed here; remaining protocol phase counts/lifetimes and source pin coverage require their existing independent reviews.
64-bit usize, nonzero element sizes, successful valid Layout sizes, ordinary runtime Vec with Global, no reserve beyond known final length. No arbitrary custom allocator guarantee.
Requested Layout bytes exclude malloc rounding, allocator metadata/internal realloc scratch, stack, process memory, provider scratch, instruction/cycle/deadline or production envelope guarantee.
